## Three ways to log, routed by a segmented control

Doc 06 gives photo, recents and manual equal billing and does not route them. They are now a three-way segmented control at the top of capture — one tap apart, no buried setting, no sheet in front of the camera.

The ordering is deliberate. Photo is first because it is the fast path for food you have never eaten before. For anything recurring it is the *wrong* path, and making Recents visible at the moment of logging is the only way a user discovers that.

**Two of the three paths make no API call and store no image.** That is the economic argument for the feature and it is stated on the screens themselves.

### Capture (9g)

The description field moved onto the capture screen, cyan-edged, directly above the shutter. Doc 06 has always said a typed description beats the photo where the two disagree, and it was missing from every prior drawing. Its label says so: `SAY WHAT IT IS · BEATS THE PHOTO`.

All image metadata is gone — no file size, no dimensions, no format. Doc 13 showed those and they are noise to a person photographing lunch.

### Recents (9h)

Distinct prior items, most recent first, with search. Expanding a row sets quantity **and shows what it adds before committing** — a re-log should never be a guess.

The footer states the mechanism plainly: your history *is* the library. There is no separate saved-foods table to build or curate.

### Manual (9i)

Name, three numbers, quantity. The escape hatch that every AI failure state in doc 18 already points at, now a real screen rather than an implied one.

The note at the bottom is the reason it is worth building properly: **a manual entry becomes a recent like any other.** Typing it once is the price of never typing it again.

---

## Review shows line items (9j)

This reverses doc 13. The estimate is a list of foods with portions and per-item macros, not one blended number.

**Totals still lead.** Three large numbers at the top; items are a quiet secondary list underneath. Line items in the model does not mean line items dominating the UI — the question a user is answering on this screen is still "does 540 look right", and only then "which line is wrong".

Adding a missed food is a dashed row at the end of the list, which routes to the same Recents picker. No separate add-item screen.

### Correction is per-item (9k)

The `±5 kcal / ±1g` steppers on all three macros are **deleted**. They asked the user to know what forty-seven calories looks like, which nobody does.

Tapping an item row expands it in place. A sheet would cover the totals, and the totals moving as you adjust *is* the feedback — that is the whole reason to correct something. Three actions live in the expanded row:

* **Quantity** — a stepper, because "there were three, not two" is the most common correction and it needs no typing.
* **Re-prompt this line** — sends one item back to the model, not the whole plate. The rest of the entry keeps the numbers it already has. Costs a quota call, and the sheet says so.
* **Remove** — for a food that was never on the plate.

**Whole-plate scaling survives** as a five-button row for when everything is proportionally off. Portion is the mental model users actually have.

### Saved without a photo (9l)

Two of three paths produce no image, so the confirmation cannot depend on one. Layout holds; the title carries it.

The old copy on this screen read *"Logged. Streak holds."* — caught and cut. Streaks left the MVP in doc 21 and this was the last live reference to them in the logging flow.

## Entry detail (9m, 9n)

**Log this again sits directly under the totals.** Doc 07 calls re-logging the highest-frequency action in the product; it costs nothing to run and it was previously not on any screen.

It creates a **new entry at the current time** rather than doubling the quantity of this one — doubling would claim both servings were eaten at 08:14, which corrupts the timeline and any future time-of-day analysis.

`9n` is the no-photo variant and the acceptance criterion easiest to miss. With no image there is no hero, so the title block carries the screen, and the estimate-versus-saved panel is absent — there was never a model response to compare against. The source badge reads `FROM RECENTS`.

Delete confirmation (`7b`, unchanged) now names every item as a consequence, and points out that fixing one line is the better move if only one line is wrong.

---

## Decisions

**No meal grouping anywhere.** Doc 12 and doc 21 flow 02 both implied breakfast / lunch / dinner / snack buckets. The list is flat and reverse-chronological. Grouping forces a classification decision on every save that most users do not care about and that the model cannot make reliably.

**Review is reachable from all three paths and looks the same from each.** Only the hero image and the back label differ (`RETAKE` versus `BACK`). One screen, three entrances.

**Confidence is only shown when there is something to be unconfident about.** Photo entries get the medium-confidence strip; recents and manual entries do not, because the numbers came from the user.

---

## Gaps and open questions

**Whole-plate scaling and per-item quantity can disagree.** Scale to 1.5×, then set an item to ×2, and it is ambiguous which multiplier the server should persist. Cleanest answer is that scaling writes through into each item's quantity immediately and then resets itself to 1× — but that is an E4 decision and it should be made before the endpoint is built, not after.

**Re-prompting one item can change what that item is.** The flow assumes a corrected portion of the same food. If the model returns a different food entirely, the line silently becomes something else. Acceptable, but it needs to be visible in the result rather than swapped underneath the user.

**Recents needs a definition of "distinct". Resolved.** Doc 02 now specifies it: distinct on (normalized name, portion_label), case-folded and whitespace-trimmed, with macros taken from the most recently logged instance. Name alone would collapse "chicken breast · 4 oz" and "chicken breast · 8 oz" into one row carrying whichever macros were logged last.
